admission.text: Holistic school-level review of curriculum, grades, trends and other credentials. No Ontario percentage admission threshold was verified.

acceptanceRate.text: No defined-cohort acceptance rate is used. Entering-class size divided by applications would be yield-related, not an acceptance rate.

sat.text: New Brunswick is test optional through 2027. Fall 2028 policy needs confirmation. Submitted scores must come from the testing agency.

satMiddle50.text: SAS: 1380–1520, middle 50% of Fall 2026 admitted students submitting scores. This school-specific distribution is neither a minimum nor a guarantee.

satTarget.text: Use the SAS distribution as submission context. A 1500 score does not prove that a 60–65% Ontario transcript meets admission standards.

deadlines.text: Fall 2028 deadlines are not verified. Fall 2027 reference: EA November 1, 2026; RD December 1, 2026; reply May 1, 2027.

application.text: Rutgers Application or Common App; USD 70 fee; required essay and STARS record. Recommendations are not requested.

ontario.text: International-school students self-report coursework and marks through STARS; official records follow for enrollment. An Ontario top-six formula, U/M equivalencies and minimum percentage were not verified.

coursework.text: SAS requires 16 academic units: English 4, one foreign language 2, mathematics 3 through Algebra II, science 2, and other academic courses 5. Confirm Ontario equivalencies.

international.text: Rutgers international guidance includes students attending high school outside the U.S.; citizenship and immigration questions still determine the relevant documentation.

english.text: For New Brunswick, IELTS 6.5 or DET 115 are listed. English-medium schooling may receive a case-by-case waiver. Do not assume Ontario attendance automatically qualifies. Pharmacy/nursing have higher requirements.

majorStructure.text: SAS students normally declare during second year, after prerequisites where applicable. Sociology requires introductory sociology plus a listed thematic course before declaration; this is a college-stage rule, not a high-school cutoff.

recommendedMajors.text: Sociology BA and History BA are genuine SAS options. No lower freshman admission cutoff or major-specific admission advantage was established.

ap.text: SAS considers official AP scores of 4 or 5 for credit, subject to subject-specific evaluation. AP credit is not a general admission requirement. Recheck the entry-year table.

cost.text: 2026–27 New Brunswick nonresident on-campus tuition, fees, food and housing: USD 62,782. This is not full international cost: insurance, SEVIS administration, books, travel and other expenses are additional.

aid.text: Admitted international first-years are automatically considered for competitive awards of USD 5,000–16,000 annually. Current renewal requires a 3.25 GPA; awards are not guaranteed. Recheck 2028 terms.

admission.text: Holistic review; secondary-school completion and university eligibility in the home country are required. No Ontario percentage cutoff was verified.

acceptanceRate.text: A Storrs-specific acceptance rate for a defined cohort was not verified; no rate is used.

sat.text: SAT/ACT are optional for the foreseeable future. UConn superscores submitted official results. Reconfirm Fall 2028 application instructions.

satMiddle50.text: Storrs Fall 2026 admitted score submitters: SAT 1320–1460. Regional-campus 970–1250 figures describe a different admission destination.

satTarget.text: Compare a submitted score with the Storrs range. A higher SAT does not establish eligibility for a low Ontario average.

deadlines.text: Fall 2028 dates not verified. Fall 2027 reference: ED November 1; merit/Honors priority December 1; Storrs deadline January 15. ED is binding; confirm its agreement before choosing it.

application.text: Common App or Coalition Application; USD 80 fee. Personal essay is required; two recommendations are optional but preferred. Official secondary records are required.

ontario.text: Canada: Grades 9–11 official records during high school; final Grades 9–12 transcript and provincial completion diploma before enrollment. No Ontario U/M or top-six minimum was verified.

coursework.text: CLAS requires 16 high-school units, including English 4, mathematics 3, one foreign language 2, lab science 2 and social science 2. Ontario equivalencies require confirmation.

international.text: International first-year instructions apply to non-U.S. citizens/non-permanent residents completing secondary school. Citizenship, not Ontario residency alone, matters.

english.text: Non-native speakers generally need proof: IELTS 6.5 or DET 110. SAT EBRW 510 can qualify for a waiver. Ontario attendance alone is not a listed blanket exemption.

majorStructure.text: CLAS offers broad BA majors. Students not directly admitted to an intended program may enter ACES; later admission to application-based majors is a separate process, not guaranteed.

recommendedMajors.text: Sociology, History and Anthropology BA are CLAS options. No evidence establishes one as the lowest-cutoff freshman major.

ap.text: The published 2025–26 table awards credit for AP English Language, Psychology and Statistics at 4/5, with course-specific awards. Recheck the entry-year policy.

cost.text: 2026–27 Storrs out-of-state direct-cost reference: USD 59,426 for tuition, standard fees, housing and meals. This is not a complete international budget; insurance, international fees and indirect expenses need separate confirmation.

aid.text: International applicants can be considered for Global Excellence and other listed merit awards. Most merit consideration is automatic; Stamps requires a supplement. Eligibility and future amounts require rechecking.

admission.text: Selective holistic review considers the full application, not a single score. No official Ontario percentage admission threshold was verified.

acceptanceRate.text: No cohort-specific acceptance percentage is used in this research.

sat.text: SAT/ACT submission is optional under current international instructions. Confirm that this remains the rule for Fall 2028.

satMiddle50.text: Fall 2025 enrolled score submitters: 1330–1480 combined SAT, 1,322 students with scores. The weighted U.S. GPA statistic is not an Ontario percentage equivalency.

satTarget.text: Use 1330–1480 as score context only. A 1500 does not waive transcript, subject or major requirements.

deadlines.text: Fall 2028 dates are not explicitly verified. Current recurring reference: EA November 5; RD January 15; enrollment deposit May 1.

application.text: Common App including UMass questions; official Grades 9–11 records; recommendation; USD 85 international fee; English evidence where required. Submit college transcripts if applicable.

ontario.text: Canada table: Grades 9–11 official transcript while in high school; after completion, Grades 9–12 plus provincial secondary diploma. No Ontario minimum average or top-six formula is stated in the reviewed table.

coursework.text: Published units: English 4; math 4 including senior-year math; lab science 3; social science 2; same foreign language 2; electives 2. Confirm Ontario equivalents, including the U.S.-history wording. Engineering, business and CS need advanced math.

international.text: UMass defines international applicants by non-immigrant visa/status, including certain pending permanent residents. Citizenship and status must be entered accurately.

english.text: First-year IELTS 6.5 with each section 6.0, or DET 115. The discretionary school waiver specifies four English-medium years with British/American curriculum; Ontario schooling is not automatically covered.

majorStructure.text: Applicants choose a major or exploratory track. SBS Anthropology has no declaration prerequisites; Sociology students can declare by meeting an advisor. These are major-declaration rules, not lower freshman admission standards.

recommendedMajors.text: Anthropology, Sociology and Political Science BA are genuine SBS options. No verified lowest-admitted Ontario average or comparative freshman-major advantage is available.

ap.text: AP can yield credit or advanced standing according to exam and score; official scores must be sent. Criteria may change. AP credit does not replace admission requirements.

cost.text: 2026–27 international 9-month estimated cost of attendance: USD 69,465, including USD 43,819 tuition/fees and listed health insurance. Program-specific fees can be additional. Not a 2028 quote.

aid.text: International undergraduates receive automatic admission-stage merit consideration but are ineligible for most financial aid. Federal aid depends on eligible citizenship/status. Merit awards are not guaranteed.

admission.text: UB expects the equivalent of U.S. GPA 3.0/B and gives 83/100 as a generic illustration. Admissions evaluates national grading systems; this is not verified as an Ontario 83% threshold.

acceptanceRate.text: No acceptance percentage is used; aggregate admission results are not a student-specific prediction.

sat.text: SAT/ACT are optional for international admission and scholarship consideration under the current policy. Confirm Fall 2028 instructions.

satMiddle50.text: Fall 2025 CDS reports SAT EBRW 610–690 and Math 610–700, but no combined-score percentile. Do not add section percentiles. Composite bins: 12% at 1000–1199, 68% at 1200–1399, 20% at 1400–1600.

satTarget.text: No composite middle-50 target is invented. The CDS bins describe score submitters only and cannot turn 1100–1500 into admission probabilities.

deadlines.text: Fall 2028 dates unconfirmed. Current fall reference: EA November 1; Honors priority December 15; RD completion February 1; later applications only while capacity remains.

application.text: ApplySUNY, Common App or Coalition; submit only one. Fee USD 50. Academic records, essay and other required materials are reviewed; non-English documents need translation. Confirm recommendation requirements in the portal.

ontario.text: UB evaluates national grading systems and requires secondary academic records. The Canada selector did not expose a verifiable Ontario U/M/top-six rule. Ask for the OSSD/course requirements and official grade assessment.

coursework.text: The 2025–26 CDS recommends 17 units: English 4, math 3, science 3, foreign language 3, social studies 4. These are recommendations, not an Ontario formula.

international.text: U.S. citizens and permanent residents educated abroad use the domestic route with foreign credentials. Other students needing U.S. study status use international instructions; confirm documentation for Canadian citizenship.

english.text: Current minimum examples: IELTS Academic 6.0, DET 105, SAT EBRW 500, or AP English Language exam 4. Scores generally must be under two years old. Ontario-school waiver is not assumed.

majorStructure.text: Indicate an intended major, with a second choice encouraged. Accounting/business direct entry is capacity limited; engineering has additional math/science review. Arts programs can require auditions or portfolios.

recommendedMajors.text: Sociology, History and Anthropology BA are available. No published Ontario freshman cutoff or evidence of the lowest-admission major was verified. Choose these for academic fit.

ap.text: UB awards advanced-standing credit based on AP/IB and other examinations. Use the current exam equivalency table; admission eligibility and credit awards are different.

cost.text: Current international Fall/Spring estimate totals USD 61,030 for the first year, including tuition, fees, insurance, housing/dining and related expenses. The related-expense footnote remains 2025–26; confirm the full entry-year budget.

aid.text: Admitted international first-years are automatically considered for variable Flagship Scholarships, renewable up to four years subject to continuing eligibility. Presidential Scholarship requires a separate application. No award is guaranteed.
